title: The truth about Joker: Folie a Deux (ending discussion)

commenti.body: So he made a soulless boring movie because people liked the version of the Joker that he made and he had to make sure this version of the Joker got his comeuppance. Don't people just like the Joker in general? Should all versions be torn down? How about other movie villains people like, should they be torn down too? How about movies that have a message people don't like, should those movies be trashed and forgotten?  What happened to the day when movies were made for enjoyment? Don't need a lecture and message in every movie. Sounds like this movie sucked and people should not waste their time or money to watch some megalomaniac try to wash his conscience clean.

Facts. If he hated the original or how people reacted to it, he could have said no to the sequel. 

But if you are going to make the sequel, at least make the effort to make it watchable and entertaining. This is a $190 million dollar movie featuring The Joker and Harley Quinn. 

Todd Phillips mistakenly believes he's a good enough director to tackle these issues in his movie. He should have stuck to ripping off Scorsese, at least that was watchable.

I think you're right, probably, but giving Phillips a bit too much credit. Audiences tend to misunderstand antiheroes, rooting for them instead of thinking critically.  The Sopranos is always the first example to come to mind. David Chase talked about needing to remind people that Tony wasn't a good guy with scenes of him doing something unforgiveable.  Breaking Bad repeatedly demonstrates that Walt is a bastard, but there were still fans getting mad at Skyler for not being jazzed about their new meth dealin' life style.  Whether it's stan culture or a media literacy issue, a lot of people just don't understand that you can enjoy the complexity of a character without stanning them.  So, I have no doubt Philips recoiled at the people who were rooting for Arthur in the first movie, but if he was half the director he thinks he is, he could have reminded us who Arthur really is while also being entertaining.

Todd Phillips is a real "I'm 14 and this is deep" sort of guy.  He's certainly a competent filmmaker and with the right team backing him can create quality work, but doesn't really have a unique creative voice of his own. His biggest hits - The Hangover and the Joker - likely wouldn't have been so memorable if not for the luck of casting Zach Galifinakis and Joaquin Phoenix. He exists somewhere between Michael Bay and Zack Snyder in the pantheon of directors, although I'd probably give those bozos more credit. Bay doesn't have any delusions of artistic grandeur, while Snyder's delusions are at least interesting.  Phillips shot a Scorcese fanfilm with the Joker and thinks he's an auteur.

People are complex and that is what people love about Tony Soprano and Walter White. Tony is a vicious killing thug, but also a loving father and husband. Walter started selling meth because he thought he was going to die and wanted to provide for his family before he was gone. Then money and power corrupted him or brought out the evil that was already in him.  Are they both evil, yes. Were they also loving and caring, also yes. Two conflicting realities can be true at the same time. They are complex characters with conflicting moral values. It's boring watching some evil person do evil things for the sake of being evil. It is not about misunderstanding anti-heroes, it is about understanding the good and evil in all of us. Even Darth Vader wasn't all evil and had a redeeming moment. Could Tony or Walter be redeemed, maybe or maybe there is nothing in them to redeem anymore, but it was fun watching them break bad.

It's such a terrible topic to discuss because you genuinely do have people idolizing characters like Tony Soprano, but I think there's an equally frustrating faction of fans who dissociate from morally bad/questionable characters as to equally miss the point entirely. 

By design, you should identify with Tony Soprano, or Pearl, or whoever. You should then question how and why they end up how they do, and be horrified at the realization that there was not some destiny that pointed them in that direction, or some unique personality quirks.
the shit that got thrown at skyler during breaking bad's run was astounding to read at the time.
